18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle. Players must use an approved paddle
that complies with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D. Players must

Approved Paddle List.

allCandidates.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered After Match Concludes
allCandidates.content:
18.A.3 Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered After Match Concludes. After
a match has ended, when a player is discovered to have used a
paddle that is not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List
or is not in compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D,
the match results stand.

allCandidates.heading: Extra Ball
allCandidates.content:
24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

allCandidates.heading: Part II: (Sections 4 through 14) applies to standard pickleball play. Section
allCandidates.content:
Part II (Sections 4 through 14) applies to standard pickleball play. Section
14 provides format variations to standard play.
See Part III for additional rules that apply to tournament play.

allCandidates.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Ball Abuse
allCandidates.content:
22.B.4 Ball Abuse. Intentionally damaging or aggressively hitting a
dead ball without endangering people.

allCandidates.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Match Forfeit – Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered During Play.
allCandidates.content:
18.A.2 Match Forfeit – Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered During Play.
During a match, when a player is discovered playing with a paddle
that is not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List or is
not in compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D, a
match forfeit will be imposed on the player.

allCandidates.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered Before Match Starts
allCandidates.content:
18.A.1 Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered Before Match Starts. Before
a match starts, when a player is discovered using a paddle that is
not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List or is not in
compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D, the player
must switch to a compliant paddle. There is no penalty to switch
paddles.

allCandidates.heading: Equipment Time-Out
allCandidates.content:
21.E Equipment Time-Out. Players are expected to keep all apparel and
equipment in playable condition.

allCandidates.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Ball Height
allCandidates.content:
7.C.3 Ball Height. The ball must clearly be no higher than the server’s
waist when the paddle contacts the ball.

allCandidates.heading: Damaged Ball
allCandidates.content:
20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a
ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

allCandidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Brand Identification
allCandidates.content:
3.C.4 Brand Identification. The ball must have a manufacturer or
supplier name or logo printed or embossed on the surface.

allCandidates.heading: 3.D.5 Prohibited Surface Features — Any other objects or features that allow a player to
allCandidates.content:
3.D.5.g Any other objects or features that allow a player to
impart excessive spin on the ball.

allCandidates.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
allCandidates.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

allCandidates.heading: Damaged Ball
allCandidates.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net Support System
allCandidates.content:
13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System. A served ball must not contact any
part of the net support system. A returned ball must not contact any part of
the net support system on the hitting player’s end of the net.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Around Net Post
allCandidates.content:
13.C Ball Around Net Post. A ball may be returned around the outside of the net
post.

allCandidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Color
allCandidates.content:
3.C.3 Color. The ball must be one uniform color, except for identification
markings. Colors may vary.

allCandidates.heading: Returned Ball Placement
allCandidates.content:
10.C Returned Ball Placement. A player must return the ball so that the ball
lands on the opponent’s end of the court or contacts the opponent or
anything that is worn or carried by the opponent before the ball lands.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net
allCandidates.content:
13.A Ball Contacting Net. When the ball contacts the net, or the rope or cable at
the top of the net between the net posts, the ball remains in play.

allCandidates.heading: 22.D Technical Fouls — Ball Abuse
allCandidates.content:
22.D.2 Ball Abuse. Aggressively or recklessly throwing or hitting a dead
ball in frustration or anger with negligent disregard for the
consequences as long as the ball does not strike a person but
puts a person at risk or in danger.

allCandidates.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
allCandidates.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

allCandidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing
allCandidates.content:
10.C.5 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing. When a player
fails to return a ball that has bounced in the player’s court before
the ball contacts a permanent object, it is a fault against that
player.

allCandidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Dead Ball
allCandidates.content:
25.B.3.d Dead Ball. When the ball strikes a permanent object
(e.g., fence, wall) before the second bounce, it is a
dead ball and the rally ends.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Under Net
allCandidates.content: 13.E Ball Under Net. A ball must not be hit under the net.

allCandidates.heading: 22.I Match Forfeit by Referee — Dangerous Paddle or Ball Abuse
allCandidates.content:
22.I.1 Dangerous Paddle or Ball Abuse. Aggressively or recklessly
striking or throwing a ball or paddle in frustration or anger that
strikes an individual or damages facility property.

originalTop.heading: LEAGUE FEES AND WAIVER
originalTop.content:
LEAGUE FEES AND WAIVER
o The registration fee is per team, per division, per season, as announced before the season
begins. No refunds will be issued starting one week before the season starts, unless a division
is canceled due to having fewer than the four-team minimum or other league-initiated
cancelations.
o The League shall provide:
 Match Balls: Franklin Outdoor X-40 optic yellow balls for all regular season and playoƯ
matches.
 DUPR Uploads: All match results logged to DUPR for rating updates (excluding mixed
and individual Picklebreaker™ games and some tournament games).
 Administration: All scheduling, website management, and administrative support.
 Championship Prize: Free entry into the following season for the Gold Medal/1st place
team in each division based on Championship Day/PlayoƯ results.
o Waiver: As an LWR PC member, you acknowledge the risks of participation and release
LWR PC, match sites, communities/clubs, and all officers/volunteers from any claims,
liability, and costs. See the full detailed Waiver here: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-ClubWaiver

allCandidates.heading: TEAM/GAME RULES
allCandidates.content:
5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.

allCandidates.heading: Damaged Ball
allCandidates.content:
20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a
ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

allCandidates.heading: Extra Ball
allCandidates.content:
24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

allCandidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Usage
allCandidates.content:
3.C.1 Usage. All approved balls are acceptable for indoor or outdoor
play. (See Figure 3-2.)

allCandidates.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Ball Height
allCandidates.content:
7.C.3 Ball Height. The ball must clearly be no higher than the server’s
waist when the paddle contacts the ball.

allCandidates.heading: USA Pickleball Approved Paddle
allCandidates.content:
18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle. Players must use an approved paddle
that complies with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D. Players must
confirm that their paddle is approved and listed on the USA Pickleball
Approved Paddle List.

allCandidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Color
allCandidates.content:
3.C.3 Color. The ball must be one uniform color, except for identification
markings. Colors may vary.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Release
allCandidates.content:
7.B Ball Release. The server must comply with Rules 7.B.1 through 7.B.3 when
releasing the ball to make the serve.

allCandidates.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
allCandidates.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

allCandidates.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Ball Abuse
allCandidates.content:
22.B.4 Ball Abuse. Intentionally damaging or aggressively hitting a
dead ball without endangering people.

allCandidates.heading: 7.B Ball Release — Release from Hand or Paddle
allCandidates.content:
7.B.1 Release from Hand or Paddle. The server must release the ball
using only one hand or only the paddle.

allCandidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Brand Identification
allCandidates.content:
3.C.4 Brand Identification. The ball must have a manufacturer or
supplier name or logo printed or embossed on the surface.

allCandidates.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Match Forfeit – Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered During Play.
allCandidates.content:
18.A.2 Match Forfeit – Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered During Play.
During a match, when a player is discovered playing with a paddle
that is not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List or is
not in compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D, a
match forfeit will be imposed on the player.

allCandidates.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered Before Match Starts
allCandidates.content:
18.A.1 Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered Before Match Starts. Before
a match starts, when a player is discovered using a paddle that is
not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List or is not in
compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D, the player
must switch to a compliant paddle. There is no penalty to switch
paddles.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net Support System
allCandidates.content:
13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System. A served ball must not contact any
part of the net support system. A returned ball must not contact any part of
the net support system on the hitting player’s end of the net.

allCandidates.heading: 22.D Technical Fouls — Ball Abuse
allCandidates.content:
22.D.2 Ball Abuse. Aggressively or recklessly throwing or hitting a dead
ball in frustration or anger with negligent disregard for the
consequences as long as the ball does not strike a person but
puts a person at risk or in danger.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Under Net
allCandidates.content: 13.E Ball Under Net. A ball must not be hit under the net.

allCandidates.heading: Damaged Ball
allCandidates.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

allCandidates.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered After Match Concludes
allCandidates.content:
18.A.3 Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered After Match Concludes. After
a match has ended, when a player is discovered to have used a
paddle that is not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List
or is not in compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D,
the match results stand.

allCandidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Dead Ball
allCandidates.content:
25.B.3.d Dead Ball. When the ball strikes a permanent object
(e.g., fence, wall) before the second bounce, it is a
dead ball and the rally ends.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Around Net Post
allCandidates.content:
13.C Ball Around Net Post. A ball may be returned around the outside of the net
post.

allCandidates.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
allCandidates.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

allCandidates.heading: Equipment Time-Out
allCandidates.content:
21.E Equipment Time-Out. Players are expected to keep all apparel and
equipment in playable condition.

allCandidates.heading: 3.B Net Specifications — Material
allCandidates.content:
3.B.1 Material. The net may be made of any mesh fabric material that
will not allow a ball to pass through it.

originalTop.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
originalTop.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
originalTop.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.

The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.

established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.

participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.

allCandidates.content:
Rally Scoring Rules
We follow standard USA Pickleball rally scoring option rules (Section 14.A) with the
following clarifications/modifications:
• Service Positioning: After a side out, the first serve is determined by the team's
score: the player on the right (baseline facing the net) serves if the score is even, and
the player on the left serves if the score is odd.
• Switching Sides: Players only switch sides after winning a point on their own serve.
The same player continues serving from the new side.
• Side Outs & Scoring: If the serving team loses a rally, a side out occurs; the
opposing team earns a point and takes over the serve.
• Game Points: A team can win a point regardless of whether they are serving or
receiving except for the winning point (see next item).
• Scoring Freeze and Match Point: To keep the game competitive through the final
point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,
a team’s score shall initially freeze at 24. The scoring freeze applies only to the team
that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using
normal Rally Scoring until it also reaches the applicable freeze point. A team must
be serving to score the game-winning point.
• Win-by-Two (2) Games: When the game is played using a win-by-two (2) format
and the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, neither team can
win by scoring the next point. Therefore, both teams’ scores shall become
unfrozen, and normal Rally Scoring shall resume. Thereafter, a team’s score shall
freeze again whenever it reaches a score at which its next point would win the

originalTop.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
originalTop.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same

allCandidates.heading: DUPR LEAGUE MANAGERS
allCandidates.content:
Rally Scoring Rules
We follow standard USA Pickleball rally scoring option rules (Section 14.A) with the
following clarifications/modifications:
• Service Positioning: After a side out, the first serve is determined by the team's
score: the player on the right (baseline facing the net) serves if the score is even, and
the player on the left serves if the score is odd.
• Switching Sides: Players only switch sides after winning a point on their own serve.
The same player continues serving from the new side.
• Side Outs & Scoring: If the serving team loses a rally, a side out occurs; the
opposing team earns a point and takes over the serve.
• Game Points: A team can win a point regardless of whether they are serving or
receiving except for the winning point (see next item).
• Scoring Freeze and Match Point: To keep the game competitive through the final
point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,
a team’s score shall initially freeze at 24. The scoring freeze applies only to the team
that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using
normal Rally Scoring until it also reaches the applicable freeze point. A team must
be serving to score the game-winning point.
• Win-by-Two (2) Games: When the game is played using a win-by-two (2) format
and the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, neither team can
win by scoring the next point. Therefore, both teams’ scores shall become
unfrozen, and normal Rally Scoring shall resume. Thereafter, a team’s score shall
freeze again whenever it reaches a score at which its next point would win the

allCandidates.content:
6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

selected.heading: Match Day Format
selected.content:
6.2.3. Match Day Format: (See table below)
6.2.3.1. All Games: Games to 15 using Rally Scoring* (win by 1). 1 point per win. Two
one-minute timeouts per team/game but no timeouts in Picklebreaker. Teams
switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points. Visitors choose serve,
receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3 and all mixed games.
6.2.3.2. Men's Round Robin: 3 Men’s teams play Round Robin (from low to high,
Teams 1 to 3). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.3. Women's Round Robin: 3 Women’s teams play Round Robin (from low to
high, Teams 4 to 6). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.4. Mixed Round: Create 6 Mixed teams (from low to high, Teams 7 to 12). Each
player will play 1 mixed game. 6 points possible.
6.2.3.5. Picklebreaker™ Game (Only played if tie at the end of all previous rounds -
12-12): Features all the mixed teams (same partners as the Mixed Round) that

selected.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
selected.content:
played in the Mixed rounds. This will be one game to 25 win by 2 using Rally
Scoring. The winning team collects 3 additional points. (If there isn’t a tie, the
leading team collects a 3-point bonus.) Note: Picklebreaker matches will not
be recorded in DUPR and do not reflect on individual’s W/L record.
6.2.3.6. DUPR Posting: All gender-based games will be submitted and posted to the
DUPR system. Mixed doubles games and any Picklebreaker™ games will not be
submitted or posted to DUPR.
Teams are numbered 1–3 for Men’s Doubles, 4–6 for Women’s Doubles, and 7–12 for Mixed
Doubles. These team numbers correspond directly to the Match Score Sheet printed from the system.
We highly recommend assigning higher team numbers to teams with higher combined skill levels and
ratings (for instance, Team 6 should have a higher combined DUPR rating than Team 4 in Women’s or
Team 12 should be a higher team rating than Team 7 in Mixed Doubles).

allCandidates.heading: Match Setup and Roster Exchange
allCandidates.content:
5.5. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within
the required timeframe may result in forfeiture of the current or future matches, at the
discretion of League Management.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Saturday League PrimeTime League

Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
[official contact omitted].
Match Setup Window

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
allCandidates.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
allCandidates.content:
ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
o The home team captain must enter all scores into the LMS within 24 hours of completing the
games. If both captains agree beforehand, the visiting team captain may enter the scores
instead.
 Entering Match Scores: To enter scores, click the Enter Match Scores button in the
match. This option becomes available only on or after the scheduled match date and
will be red.
 Forfeits and Weather Delays: If an entire match date is forfeited or canceled due to
weather, notify League Management. They will log the information for that match and
update the standings.
 Score Entry Process: When entering scores, use the dropdown menus to select the
players for each game (built from your Match Setup), then enter the scores in each
game block. Click Submit when finished; the system will check for errors before saving.
 Score Verification: Once scores are submitted, the opposing captain will receive an
email request to verify them, and a red notification count will appear in their Pending
Match Verifications block. The opposing captain must open the match, review the
scores, and click the verification button (or dispute button if they don’t accept the
scores as written). Both captains will then be notified, and the standings will update
automatically.
o The visiting team captain must verify match scores promptly. This ensures there is enough time
to review the results and enter them into DUPR before the end of the weekend.

Submitting Scores
Clicking Submit Scores saves the match results only when all player, team, and score
information is valid according to division rules. You cannot save any of the results (partial
save) if any information is invalid.
Once submitted:
• Notifications: The system automatically emails the opposing captains to notify
them that the scores have been entered.
• Verification: If your team is the first to enter the results, a captain of the opposing
team must log in to verify or dispute the scores to finalize the match and update the
league/division standings.
Score Verification Process
Use Pending Verification to review entered scores or raise disputes.
Selecting the appropriate button will:
• Finalize Results: Complete the scoring process for the match.
• Notify Captains: Automatically email all captains to confirm the match date and
scores are officially entered and locked.
• Update Standings: Instantly refresh the league/division standings.
Captain Dashboard / Pending Score Verification (red)

Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
The schedule uses two courts for men’s teams and two courts for women’s teams. After the first four
gender-doubles rounds, Men’s Team 3 and Women’s Team 6 play while Mixed Teams 7 and 8 begin.
Round 6 includes the remaining mixed teams. If the match is tied 12-12 after all gender and mixed
doubles, the Picklebreaker is played on two courts using the same mixed teams in the captains’
designated order.

for any reasonable cause based on the referee's own observation or the
unanimous request of the players.

partner change after the partners start team play is prohibited.

allCandidates.heading: End Change Time-Out
allCandidates.content:
21.B End Change Time-Out. The referee will call a time-out to allow players to
change ends at specified points during single-game matches and tie-
breaker games. Players will not change ends during the tie-breaker game
when the first game of the match was forfeited due to late arrival.
21.B.1 11-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 11
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 6.
21.B.2 15-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 15
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 8.
21.B.3 21-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 21
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 11.

Appendix B Rulebook Priorities and Guiding
Principles
Preface
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook is the organization’s most important product.
It is the foundational document for the sport of pickleball and should be treated
with the respect accorded the sport’s founders and those who have written and
approved rules over the years.
Writing rules that are objective, clear, and concise is difficult work. Because those
involved in writing and/or approving rules come from diverse backgrounds and
experiences, it is important to have rule writing priorities and guiding principles
that help provide a measure of consistency from year to year. The following
Rulebook Priorities and Guiding Principles were developed to guide rule writers and
approvers in their important work.
Priorities
The following three priorities should be considered “tests” for any suggested rule
change. Any suggested rule change should satisfy at least one of these three
priorities, listed in order of importance:
1. The first priority is preserving the integrity of the sport, one that incorporates
the elements of fun, cooperation, courtesy, and competition. This priority pays
homage to those who developed the sport in 1965 and those who have written
and approved rule changes over the years.
2. The second priority is what is collectively best for the players. This priority
examines rule changes for improving the player’s experience. It “tests”
suggested rule changes from the standpoint of minimizing player
disagreements, making it easier to learn the sport, teach the sport, and play
the sport, while also allowing for moderate innovation as player skills and
equipment develop and evolve.
3. The third priority is what is best for officiating. It “tests” rule changes to make it
less likely conflicts will occur between players as well as between players and
officials.
Guiding Principles
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook contains a wide variety of rules that cover the
court and equipment, recreational and social play as well as tournament play,
officiated and non-officiated. The following are Guiding Principles for those writing
and approving rules. To the extent possible, rules should:
1. Apply to all levels and categories of players: recreational and social players, as
well as professional and amateur tournament players (officiated and non-
officiated). Specific rules for a single category of player, for example, the pro
level player, should be approved after careful consideration and examination
of how the rule change might impact the sport beyond the pro level of
competition.
2. Be written with a deterministic focus, i.e., from the standpoint of “if this occurs,
this is what happens.” If something is not allowed or should not happen, the
consequences (for example: replay, fault, technical warning, etc.) should be
provided as part of the rule (e.g., replay, fault, technical warning, etc.).
3. Center on that which should not occur, not on what is permitted or allowed.
Attempts to include rules describing what is allowed will result in an
unnecessarily lengthy Rulebook.
4. Avoid ambiguity, player discretion, or referee judgment-related rules. Such
rules invite disagreements and different interpretations. To this end, when a
key word is used to describe when a rule applies, the word should be defined
as either a part of the rule or in the Definition section of the Rulebook.
5. Allow equipment manufacturers to innovate, as long as such innovation does
not overwhelm or outpace the average player’s ability to keep up with the
speed and difficulty of the sport. Equipment-related rule changes should be
given particularly close scrutiny because of their precedent-setting potential.
6. Have an element of precedent accorded to them. Change for change’s sake
should be avoided to avoid frustration among, or a loss of confidence by,
players.
7. Allow for an appropriate degree of player innovation. Such innovation should
maintain a healthy balance between historical rules that have been
instrumental to the sport’s growth and appeal.
8. Preserve the unique features and rules of the sport involving the Non-Volley
Zone and the two-bounce rule and prevent one shot, one paddle, or one type
of play from dominating the sport.
9. Address a known issue or anticipate trends and needs of the sport before
problems develop.
10. Be subjected to reviews and comments by domestic and international
stakeholders.

Viewing Your Play History
My Play History lets a player review their recorded league match results and performance
across the league.
Use the Play History Scope list to choose which results to view:
• All Seasons/All Teams
• A specific season, league, division, or team
The page updates immediately to show only results within the selected scope.
At the top, summary cards show:
• Games Played — the number of recorded match-line results in the selected scope.
• Wins — recorded individual line wins.
• Losses — recorded individual line losses.
• Other Category - Tracks non-counting personal games, such as forfeits and
Picklebreaker matches. Scores Pending — matches whose scores have not yet been
entered and posted.
Below the summary, each match shows the match date, teams, home/away status, season,
league, division, lines played, and available game scores. A match that still needs scoring is
clearly labeled Scores Not Entered rather than being shown as an unclear “Other” result.
Select More Player Details in the header to open a separate, scrollable details window. It
provides five additional groups of scope-specific information:
• Matches: wins, losses, and match win percentage.
• Games: individual game wins, losses, and game win percentage.
• Points: points earned, points against, and point differential percentage.
• Ratings: average recorded partner and opponent ratings, plus adjusted and overall
performance estimates.
• Last 5 Matchups: the player’s five most recent results, marked with W or L.
The details window is designed for mobile as well as desktop and can be closed without
changing the selected History Scope.
• Mobile Shortcut: Tap the Play History icon in the bottom navigation bar.

allCandidates.heading: Definitions
allCandidates.content:
Section 2 Definitions
Ball In Play. The timeframe during which a rally is played, from when the serve is
hit until the ball becomes dead.
Carry. Hitting the ball in such a way that it does not bounce away from the paddle
but is carried along on the face of the paddle.
Coaching. Communication of information (including verbal, nonverbal, and
electronic) from someone other than a player’s partner, that players may act upon
to gain an advantage or help them avoid a rules violation.
Court. The area inside the outer dimensions of the baselines and sidelines.
Dead Ball. A ball that is no longer in play.
Distraction. Physical actions by a player that are not common to the game and
interfere with the opponent’s ability or concentration to hit the ball. Examples
include, but are not limited to, making loud noises, stomping feet, and
waving the paddle in an erratic manner.
Double Bounce. When the ball bounces twice on one end of the net before it is
returned.
Double Hit. Hitting the ball twice before it is returned.
Drop Serve. A serve made by dropping the ball and hitting the ball with the paddle
after the ball bounces on the playing surface.
Ejection. Removal of a player from tournament competition for a flagrant or
injurious behavioral violation.
Expulsion. Banishment of a player from the tournament venue for a flagrant or
injurious behavioral violation.
Fault. A rules violation that results in a dead ball and the loss of a rally.
First Server (Doubles). The player who begins the team’s service rotation from
the right serving area after a side out.
Forfeit. The awarding of a game or a match to the opponent due to a violation of
the rules.
Hinder. Any transient element or occurrence not caused by a player that adversely
impacts play. Examples include, but are not limited to, stray balls, flying insects,

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club Code of Conduct
allCandidates.content:
1. Standard of Play & Sportsmanship
• Golden Rule: Treat every player, regardless of skill level, with the same respect you
expect to receive.
• Positive Environment: Support your partners and remain respectful to your
opponents. Avoid "trash talk" that crosses the line into being mean-spirited or
discouraging.
• Integrity of the Game: Players must make line calls that are "clear and certain." In
accordance with standard pickleball officiating, all "close" calls must be resolved in
favor of the opponent.
• Player Integrity: Any attempt to manipulate ratings through "sandbagging,"
reporting false scores, or intentionally losing matches is strictly prohibited and
grounds for immediate expulsion.
• On-Court Decorum: Profanity, paddle throwing, or aggressive physical gestures
toward opponents, partners, or spectators will not be tolerated.

Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.

[official contact omitted].

CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.

separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

allCandidates.heading: ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
allCandidates.content:
ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
o The home team captain must enter all scores into the LMS within 24 hours of completing the
games. If both captains agree beforehand, the visiting team captain may enter the scores
instead.
 Entering Match Scores: To enter scores, click the Enter Match Scores button in the
match. This option becomes available only on or after the scheduled match date and
will be red.
 Forfeits and Weather Delays: If an entire match date is forfeited or canceled due to
weather, notify League Management. They will log the information for that match and
update the standings.
 Score Entry Process: When entering scores, use the dropdown menus to select the
players for each game (built from your Match Setup), then enter the scores in each
game block. Click Submit when finished; the system will check for errors before saving.
 Score Verification: Once scores are submitted, the opposing captain will receive an
email request to verify them, and a red notification count will appear in their Pending
Match Verifications block. The opposing captain must open the match, review the
scores, and click the verification button (or dispute button if they don’t accept the
scores as written). Both captains will then be notified, and the standings will update
automatically.
o The visiting team captain must verify match scores promptly. This ensures there is enough time
to review the results and enter them into DUPR before the end of the weekend.

Submitting Scores
Clicking Submit Scores saves the match results only when all player, team, and score
information is valid according to division rules. You cannot save any of the results (partial
save) if any information is invalid.
Once submitted:
• Notifications: The system automatically emails the opposing captains to notify
them that the scores have been entered.
• Verification: If your team is the first to enter the results, a captain of the opposing
team must log in to verify or dispute the scores to finalize the match and update the
league/division standings.
Score Verification Process
Use Pending Verification to review entered scores or raise disputes.
Selecting the appropriate button will:
• Finalize Results: Complete the scoring process for the match.
• Notify Captains: Automatically email all captains to confirm the match date and
scores are officially entered and locked.
• Update Standings: Instantly refresh the league/division standings.

Appendix B Rulebook Priorities and Guiding
Principles
Preface
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook is the organization’s most important product.
It is the foundational document for the sport of pickleball and should be treated
with the respect accorded the sport’s founders and those who have written and
approved rules over the years.
Writing rules that are objective, clear, and concise is difficult work. Because those
involved in writing and/or approving rules come from diverse backgrounds and
experiences, it is important to have rule writing priorities and guiding principles
that help provide a measure of consistency from year to year. The following
Rulebook Priorities and Guiding Principles were developed to guide rule writers and
approvers in their important work.
Priorities
The following three priorities should be considered “tests” for any suggested rule
change. Any suggested rule change should satisfy at least one of these three
priorities, listed in order of importance:
1. The first priority is preserving the integrity of the sport, one that incorporates
the elements of fun, cooperation, courtesy, and competition. This priority pays
homage to those who developed the sport in 1965 and those who have written
and approved rule changes over the years.
2. The second priority is what is collectively best for the players. This priority
examines rule changes for improving the player’s experience. It “tests”
suggested rule changes from the standpoint of minimizing player
disagreements, making it easier to learn the sport, teach the sport, and play
the sport, while also allowing for moderate innovation as player skills and
equipment develop and evolve.
3. The third priority is what is best for officiating. It “tests” rule changes to make it
less likely conflicts will occur between players as well as between players and
officials.
Guiding Principles
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook contains a wide variety of rules that cover the
court and equipment, recreational and social play as well as tournament play,
officiated and non-officiated. The following are Guiding Principles for those writing
and approving rules. To the extent possible, rules should:
1. Apply to all levels and categories of players: recreational and social players, as
well as professional and amateur tournament players (officiated and non-
officiated). Specific rules for a single category of player, for example, the pro
level player, should be approved after careful consideration and examination
of how the rule change might impact the sport beyond the pro level of
competition.
2. Be written with a deterministic focus, i.e., from the standpoint of “if this occurs,
this is what happens.” If something is not allowed or should not happen, the
consequences (for example: replay, fault, technical warning, etc.) should be
provided as part of the rule (e.g., replay, fault, technical warning, etc.).
3. Center on that which should not occur, not on what is permitted or allowed.
Attempts to include rules describing what is allowed will result in an
unnecessarily lengthy Rulebook.
4. Avoid ambiguity, player discretion, or referee judgment-related rules. Such
rules invite disagreements and different interpretations. To this end, when a
key word is used to describe when a rule applies, the word should be defined
as either a part of the rule or in the Definition section of the Rulebook.
5. Allow equipment manufacturers to innovate, as long as such innovation does
not overwhelm or outpace the average player’s ability to keep up with the
speed and difficulty of the sport. Equipment-related rule changes should be
given particularly close scrutiny because of their precedent-setting potential.
6. Have an element of precedent accorded to them. Change for change’s sake
should be avoided to avoid frustration among, or a loss of confidence by,
players.
7. Allow for an appropriate degree of player innovation. Such innovation should
maintain a healthy balance between historical rules that have been
instrumental to the sport’s growth and appeal.
8. Preserve the unique features and rules of the sport involving the Non-Volley
Zone and the two-bounce rule and prevent one shot, one paddle, or one type
of play from dominating the sport.
9. Address a known issue or anticipate trends and needs of the sport before
problems develop.
10. Be subjected to reviews and comments by domestic and international
stakeholders.

allCandidates.heading: Definitions
allCandidates.content:
Section 2 Definitions
Ball In Play. The timeframe during which a rally is played, from when the serve is
hit until the ball becomes dead.
Carry. Hitting the ball in such a way that it does not bounce away from the paddle
but is carried along on the face of the paddle.
Coaching. Communication of information (including verbal, nonverbal, and
electronic) from someone other than a player’s partner, that players may act upon
to gain an advantage or help them avoid a rules violation.
Court. The area inside the outer dimensions of the baselines and sidelines.
Dead Ball. A ball that is no longer in play.
Distraction. Physical actions by a player that are not common to the game and
interfere with the opponent’s ability or concentration to hit the ball. Examples
include, but are not limited to, making loud noises, stomping feet, and
waving the paddle in an erratic manner.
Double Bounce. When the ball bounces twice on one end of the net before it is
returned.
Double Hit. Hitting the ball twice before it is returned.
Drop Serve. A serve made by dropping the ball and hitting the ball with the paddle
after the ball bounces on the playing surface.
Ejection. Removal of a player from tournament competition for a flagrant or
injurious behavioral violation.
Expulsion. Banishment of a player from the tournament venue for a flagrant or
injurious behavioral violation.
Fault. A rules violation that results in a dead ball and the loss of a rally.
First Server (Doubles). The player who begins the team’s service rotation from
the right serving area after a side out.
Forfeit. The awarding of a game or a match to the opponent due to a violation of
the rules.
Hinder. Any transient element or occurrence not caused by a player that adversely
impacts play. Examples include, but are not limited to, stray balls, flying insects,

Viewing Your Play History
My Play History lets a player review their recorded league match results and performance
across the league.
Use the Play History Scope list to choose which results to view:
• All Seasons/All Teams
• A specific season, league, division, or team
The page updates immediately to show only results within the selected scope.
At the top, summary cards show:
• Games Played — the number of recorded match-line results in the selected scope.
• Wins — recorded individual line wins.
• Losses — recorded individual line losses.
• Other Category - Tracks non-counting personal games, such as forfeits and
Picklebreaker matches. Scores Pending — matches whose scores have not yet been
entered and posted.
Below the summary, each match shows the match date, teams, home/away status, season,
league, division, lines played, and available game scores. A match that still needs scoring is
clearly labeled Scores Not Entered rather than being shown as an unclear “Other” result.
Select More Player Details in the header to open a separate, scrollable details window. It
provides five additional groups of scope-specific information:
• Matches: wins, losses, and match win percentage.
• Games: individual game wins, losses, and game win percentage.
• Points: points earned, points against, and point differential percentage.
• Ratings: average recorded partner and opponent ratings, plus adjusted and overall
performance estimates.
• Last 5 Matchups: the player’s five most recent results, marked with W or L.
The details window is designed for mobile as well as desktop and can be closed without
changing the selected History Scope.
• Mobile Shortcut: Tap the Play History icon in the bottom navigation bar.

Player Dashboard Main Screen (Mobile view)
The mobile version includes two unique navigation areas not found on desktop:
• Top Menu: Click or tap the “hamburger” (☰) icon to open the main navigation
menu. From there, you can switch between teams, view your play history, check
division schedules and standings, or access the latest league documents.
• Top Navigation: Switch your Dashboard view (if you are also a captain) or change
your Active Team (if you are a member of multiple teams).
• Bottom Navigation: Quickly access key menu items via a shortcut bar at the bottom
of the screen.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club Code of Conduct
allCandidates.content:
1. Standard of Play & Sportsmanship
• Golden Rule: Treat every player, regardless of skill level, with the same respect you
expect to receive.
• Positive Environment: Support your partners and remain respectful to your
opponents. Avoid "trash talk" that crosses the line into being mean-spirited or
discouraging.
• Integrity of the Game: Players must make line calls that are "clear and certain." In
accordance with standard pickleball officiating, all "close" calls must be resolved in
favor of the opponent.
• Player Integrity: Any attempt to manipulate ratings through "sandbagging,"
reporting false scores, or intentionally losing matches is strictly prohibited and
grounds for immediate expulsion.
• On-Court Decorum: Profanity, paddle throwing, or aggressive physical gestures
toward opponents, partners, or spectators will not be tolerated.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: CAPTAINS NORMAL WEEKLY PROCESS
allCandidates.content:
CAPTAINS NORMAL WEEKLY PROCESS
o Captain Match Duties: For every match, captains or co-captains must set their lineup (Match
Setup), print the score sheet, and enter or validate final scores.
o Lineup Submission: Both captains must enter starting lineups in Match Setup at least 3 days
before match day. It is recommended that the Home Team enter their lineups first.
 Updates: You can modify your lineup until match day. The system automatically emails
changes to the opposing captain.
 Penalties: Repeated incomplete or late lineup submissions may result in match
forfeiture, subject to League Management discretion.
o Match Score Sheet: Once both teams have entered their lineups in the League Management
System (LMS), the official Match Score Sheet may be printed. Captains can access the Match
Score Sheet button from the “Next Match” section of their Captain Dashboard.
 The completed Match Score Sheet will include all available match information,
including player names, team information, and game formats. If either team has not
entered its lineup, that team’s lineup information will appear blank on the score
sheet.
 The LMS-generated Match Score Sheet is the official score sheet and must be used
for each scheduled match. Captains should retain all completed Match Score
Sheets for the duration of the season as a backup record of match results.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
allCandidates.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages
allCandidates.content:
5.14. Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages: If weather or other factors interrupt
play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.14.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.
5.14.2. At least half of the games are completed: Completed results will stand. Any
remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).
5.14.3. Roster Continuity: When a game is rescheduled, the players originally assigned to
it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.

6.2.5. Player Cap: Every player plays 3 gender double games to 15 and will then play 1
mixed game to 15. Optional lineups may include players who compete only in
gender doubles or only in mixed doubles. Depending on the outcome, the 6 mixed
teams will then play the Picklebreaker sequence playing up to 4+ points per team.

Viewing My Teams Information
If you are on multiple teams, you can easily switch between them. Go to the sidebar, select
My Team, and choose the team you want to see.
The team page displays:
• Next Match: Shows at the top with quick links to Match Details and Match Lineup
(if available).
• Team Performance: Displays your team's current record, rank and your personal
season DUPR rating.
• Schedules & Results: Lists of upcoming matches and recent match results.
• Team Roster: Shows your full roster. Tap or click any captain's card to email them
directly.
• League Documents: Access all current league files via the sidebar option.
For more details, see the sections below on Team Roster, Division Standings, and Team
Matches.

Upcoming Matches
Your Next Match appears at the top of the Captain Dashboard. From this section, captains
can view match details, email the opposing captains, print Match Score Sheet and enter final
scores. If this is a “flex league” you are also able to modify the match date/time and notify
opposing captains.
You can also manage your match lineup and score sheets here:
• Match Setup block: The Match Setup button turns red if your team hasn't entered
its lineup yet, and blue once you have. The system will email you a reminder to
complete this a few days before the actual match.
• Print Match Score Sheet button: Stays red until both teams complete their Match
Setup, turning green and ready to print once both lineups are in.
The Upcoming matches & byes section shows all upcoming match details, scheduling
information, and setup status. You can also click on a match for all available tools/options
for that match.

The Lineups: Captains determine the lineup order, making strategy an important part of the

allCandidates.content: Section 18 Player Pre-Match

Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
[official contact omitted].

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.content:
6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Scoring
allCandidates.content:
6.1.4. Scoring: Each win earns 1 point with 9 total possible match points per date.
6.1.5. Player Cap: Each player plays exactly 3 games to 15.
6.1.6. Teams may use two doubles teams if they inform their opponents in advance. If a
team lacks a third doubles team, they must forfeit those 3 games and points. In this
case, the community team with three teams will play against the other two.

finalTop.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
finalTop.heading: Match Setup and Roster Exchange
finalTop.content:
5.5. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within
the required timeframe may result in forfeiture of the current or future matches, at the
discretion of League Management.

finalTop.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
finalTop.heading: Scheduling
finalTop.content:
6.2.1. Scheduling: Games are typically scheduled for every other Saturday at noon.
6.2.2. Roster & Courts: 12 players—6 men and 6 women—divided into six teams: 3 men’s
doubles teams and 3 women’s doubles teams. Mixed teams may be formed from
the gender doubles players or can be from additional players who participate only in
the mixed round. Requires 4 courts.

The schedule uses two courts for men’s teams and two courts for women’s teams. After the first four

designated order.

will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within
the required timeframe may result in forfeiture of the current or future matches, at the
discretion of League Management.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
allCandidates.content:
Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
The schedule uses two courts for men’s teams and two courts for women’s teams. After the first four
gender-doubles rounds, Men’s Team 3 and Women’s Team 6 play while Mixed Teams 7 and 8 begin.
Round 6 includes the remaining mixed teams. If the match is tied 12-12 after all gender and mixed
doubles, the Picklebreaker is played on two courts using the same mixed teams in the captains’
designated order.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Scheduling
allCandidates.content:
6.3.1. Scheduling: Women’s and men’s games are typically scheduled for Fridays at
noon.
6.3.2. Roster & Courts: 4 players / 2 lines. Requires 2 courts. Player age is determined as
of 12/31 of the season’s starting year. Players must be 65 or older and will use the
DUPR Age-Based Rating. Players who are under age 65 at the start of the season
but will turn 65 by December 31 of the current calendar year shall be considered
Not Rated (NR) for purposes of their Season DUPR Rating, as they will not yet have
an official 65+ age-based DUPR rating at the start of the season.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
allCandidates.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

one-minute timeouts per team/game but no timeouts in Picklebreaker. Teams

receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3 and all mixed games.

Teams 1 to 3). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.

6.2.3.4. Mixed Round: Create 6 Mixed teams (from low to high, Teams 7 to 12). Each
player will play 1 mixed game. 6 points possible.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: CAPTAINS NORMAL WEEKLY PROCESS
allCandidates.content:
CAPTAINS NORMAL WEEKLY PROCESS
o Captain Match Duties: For every match, captains or co-captains must set their lineup (Match
Setup), print the score sheet, and enter or validate final scores.
o Lineup Submission: Both captains must enter starting lineups in Match Setup at least 3 days
before match day. It is recommended that the Home Team enter their lineups first.
 Updates: You can modify your lineup until match day. The system automatically emails
changes to the opposing captain.
 Penalties: Repeated incomplete or late lineup submissions may result in match
forfeiture, subject to League Management discretion.
o Match Score Sheet: Once both teams have entered their lineups in the League Management
System (LMS), the official Match Score Sheet may be printed. Captains can access the Match
Score Sheet button from the “Next Match” section of their Captain Dashboard.
 The completed Match Score Sheet will include all available match information,
including player names, team information, and game formats. If either team has not
entered its lineup, that team’s lineup information will appear blank on the score
sheet.
 The LMS-generated Match Score Sheet is the official score sheet and must be used
for each scheduled match. Captains should retain all completed Match Score
Sheets for the duration of the season as a backup record of match results.

allCandidates.heading: Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions
allCandidates.content:
5.6. Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions: All active players must appear on the
team’s roster in the LMS prior to match play. Retroactive additions are permitted without
penalty only if the player is a valid LWR PC member with an eligible DUPR account and
rating. Failure to meet these requirements will result in a match forfeit, and the match will
not be posted to DUPR.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: LEAGUE FEES AND WAIVER
allCandidates.content:
LEAGUE FEES AND WAIVER
o The registration fee is per team, per division, per season, as announced before the season
begins. No refunds will be issued starting one week before the season starts, unless a division
is canceled due to having fewer than the four-team minimum or other league-initiated
cancelations.
o The League shall provide:
 Match Balls: Franklin Outdoor X-40 optic yellow balls for all regular season and playoƯ
matches.
 DUPR Uploads: All match results logged to DUPR for rating updates (excluding mixed
and individual Picklebreaker™ games and some tournament games).
 Administration: All scheduling, website management, and administrative support.
 Championship Prize: Free entry into the following season for the Gold Medal/1st place
team in each division based on Championship Day/PlayoƯ results.
o Waiver: As an LWR PC member, you acknowledge the risks of participation and release
LWR PC, match sites, communities/clubs, and all officers/volunteers from any claims,
liability, and costs. See the full detailed Waiver here: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-ClubWaiver

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: VIEW SCHEDULE/GAME INFORMATION
allCandidates.content:
VIEW SCHEDULE/GAME INFORMATION
o On the Captain Dashboard, the selected team’s “next match” will be displayed along with
options for that match.
o Match Setup & Lineups: Captains must enter their lineups before match day to verify player
and team ratings. For complete details, see the Team/Game Rules in the DUPR League Rules.
o Completed Matches: Scroll down to the Recent results section to review score details for
past matches. Click on a match to see all detailed results including players and individual game
scores.
o Court Reservations & Match Details: The home team captain must reserve the required
number of courts for warm-ups and match play. You should confirm the start time and share all
location details with the visiting captain beforehand by clicking the Email Opposing Captains
button.
o Finding Captain Contact Info: Click the Division Captains button in the Captain Tools block
to view or print contact details for all captains and co-captains in your division.

Upcoming Matches
Your Next Match appears at the top of the Captain Dashboard. From this section, captains
can view match details, email the opposing captains, print Match Score Sheet and enter final
scores. If this is a “flex league” you are also able to modify the match date/time and notify
opposing captains.
You can also manage your match lineup and score sheets here:
• Match Setup block: The Match Setup button turns red if your team hasn't entered
its lineup yet, and blue once you have. The system will email you a reminder to
complete this a few days before the actual match.
• Print Match Score Sheet button: Stays red until both teams complete their Match
Setup, turning green and ready to print once both lineups are in.
The Upcoming matches & byes section shows all upcoming match details, scheduling
information, and setup status. You can also click on a match for all available tools/options
for that match.
Upcoming / Unverified Matches Screen

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages
allCandidates.content:
5.14. Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages: If weather or other factors interrupt
play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.14.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.
5.14.2. At least half of the games are completed: Completed results will stand. Any
remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).
5.14.3. Roster Continuity: When a game is rescheduled, the players originally assigned to
it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.

Viewing My Teams Information
If you are on multiple teams, you can easily switch between them. Go to the sidebar, select
My Team, and choose the team you want to see.
The team page displays:
• Next Match: Shows at the top with quick links to Match Details and Match Lineup
(if available).
• Team Performance: Displays your team's current record, rank and your personal
season DUPR rating.
• Schedules & Results: Lists of upcoming matches and recent match results.
• Team Roster: Shows your full roster. Tap or click any captain's card to email them
directly.
• League Documents: Access all current league files via the sidebar option.
For more details, see the sections below on Team Roster, Division Standings, and Team
Matches.
