allCandidates.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — Before Start of Match
allCandidates.content:
21.A.1 Before Start of Match. A standard time-out cannot be called
before a match starts.

allCandidates.heading: Extending Time to Report to Match
allCandidates.content:
16.M Extending Time to Report to Match. The Tournament Director may allow
an extension of time for players to report to a match when circumstances
warrant.

allCandidates.heading: Notice of Schedule Changes
allCandidates.content:
16.L Notice of Schedule Changes. When any change is made to the tournament
schedule of matches after the initial posting, the Tournament Director must
notify the players of the changes.

allCandidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Before Start of Match
allCandidates.content:
21.C.1 Before Start of Match. A medical time-out cannot be called
before the start of a match.

allCandidates.heading: Time-Out Between Games
allCandidates.content:
21.F Time-Out Between Games. The referee will call a time-out between
games of a match.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: VIEW SCHEDULE/GAME INFORMATION
allCandidates.content:
o League Communication: For scheduling issues or other league questions, contact the league
managers by clicking the Contact League (email icon) button at the top of the screen.
o Match Balls & Score Sheets: The home team captain must bring league-provided balls to the
match and record all scores on a printed Match Score Sheet. Keep these physical score sheets
on file for the remainder of the season.

allCandidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Match Retirement
allCandidates.content:
21.C.9 Match Retirement. A match retirement is imposed when a
player is not able to continue play after the 15-minute medical
time-out period expires. A player may use their available
standard time-outs to allow more time before the match must
be retired (Rule 21.A.4). In doubles, if the retiring player's partner
decides to continue, the match will resume following all
applicable rules. The retiring player must leave the playing
surface.

allCandidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Number Available
allCandidates.content:
21.C.3 Number Available. A player may be granted only one medical
time-out per match.

Viewing Your Play History
My Play History lets a player review their recorded league match results and performance
across the league.
Use the Play History Scope list to choose which results to view:
• All Seasons/All Teams
• A specific season, league, division, or team
The page updates immediately to show only results within the selected scope.
At the top, summary cards show:
• Games Played — the number of recorded match-line results in the selected scope.
• Wins — recorded individual line wins.
• Losses — recorded individual line losses.
• Other Category - Tracks non-counting personal games, such as forfeits and
Picklebreaker matches. Scores Pending — matches whose scores have not yet been
entered and posted.
Below the summary, each match shows the match date, teams, home/away status, season,
league, division, lines played, and available game scores. A match that still needs scoring is
clearly labeled Scores Not Entered rather than being shown as an unclear “Other” result.
Select More Player Details in the header to open a separate, scrollable details window. It
provides five additional groups of scope-specific information:
• Matches: wins, losses, and match win percentage.
• Games: individual game wins, losses, and game win percentage.
• Points: points earned, points against, and point differential percentage.
• Ratings: average recorded partner and opponent ratings, plus adjusted and overall
performance estimates.
• Last 5 Matchups: the player’s five most recent results, marked with W or L.
The details window is designed for mobile as well as desktop and can be closed without
changing the selected History Scope.
• Mobile Shortcut: Tap the Play History icon in the bottom navigation bar.

allCandidates.heading: End Change Time-Out
allCandidates.content:
21.B End Change Time-Out. The referee will call a time-out to allow players to
change ends at specified points during single-game matches and tie-
breaker games. Players will not change ends during the tie-breaker game
when the first game of the match was forfeited due to late arrival.
21.B.1 11-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 11
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 6.
21.B.2 15-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 15
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 8.
21.B.3 21-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 21
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 11.

allCandidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Time Start
allCandidates.content:
21.C.7 Time Start. When medical assistance arrives, the referee will
start a 15-minute timer. Play must resume as soon as possible
but no later than 15 minutes of elapsed time.

allCandidates.heading: Time-Outs and Breaks
allCandidates.content: Section 21 Time-Outs and Breaks

allCandidates.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Change of Starting Server
allCandidates.content:
21.F.3 Change of Starting Server. Teams may change the starting
server between games and should notify the referee before the
start of the next game.

allCandidates.heading: Standard Time-Out
allCandidates.content:
21.A Standard Time-Out. Two standard time-outs are allowed per singles
player or doubles team for each 11-point and 15-point game and three
time-outs for a 21-point game.

allCandidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Valid Medical Condition
allCandidates.content:
21.C.8 Valid Medical Condition. When medical personnel, or the
Tournament Director, when medical personnel are not available,
determine that a valid medical condition exists, the player must
be able to resume play in 15 minutes or less. When the player is
able to resume play in fewer than 15 minutes, the remaining
medical time is lost and no longer available to the player during
the match.

allCandidates.heading: Medical Time-Out
allCandidates.content:
21.C Medical Time-Out. A player needing medical attention during a match,
including between games, may request a medical time-out.

allCandidates.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — Between Games
allCandidates.content:
21.A.3 Between Games. Between games, players may request to use
one or both standard time-outs before the start of the next
game. The players must inform the referee. The standard time-
out will start immediately after the expiration of the time-out
between games. A time-out must be charged when any portion
of the time is used. When the requesting singles player or
doubles team is ready to resume play before a requested time-
out begins, that time-out is not charged.

allCandidates.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Resuming Play
allCandidates.content:
21.F.4 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

allCandidates.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Time-Outs
allCandidates.content:
17.D.15 Time-Outs. Enforce time-out procedures. (See Section 21.)
17.D.16 15-Second Warnings. Announce when there are 15 seconds
remaining in a time-out. At the end of the 15 seconds, the referee
must call “time in” and then the score when all players are ready
to play or should be ready to play.

allCandidates.heading: 21.D Referee Time-Out — Resuming Play
allCandidates.content:
21.D.4 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

allCandidates.heading: 21.E Equipment Time-Out — Time-Out Award
allCandidates.content:
21.E.1 Time-Out Award. When the referee determines that an
equipment change or adjustment is necessary for fair and safe
continuation of the match, the referee may award an equipment
time-out of reasonable duration.

allCandidates.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Duration
allCandidates.content:
21.F.1 Duration. A maximum of two minutes is allowed to change ends
between games.

allCandidates.heading: Use of Time-Outs Between Games
allCandidates.content:
24.E Use of Time-Outs Between Games. Players must notify the opponent of
their intent to use one or both standard time-outs before the start of the
next game. (Modifies Rule 21.A.3)

allCandidates.content:
3. PLAYER REQUIREMENTS
3.1. All League players must have a signed/accepted waiver with LWR PC and have a valid
LWR PC membership. To sign up, go to https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup/.
3.2. All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be found at:

3.3. All DUPR League players must join our free DUPR club, which is diƯerent/separate from
the LWR PC membership: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB
3.4. Players are assigned to a community based on their primary address at the start of the
season.
3.5. Players may join teams from other communities; however, they are strongly encouraged
to play for their local community’s team when their community has a team participating in
the same league and division with available roster space.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
allCandidates.content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor of 29 or below will be classified as “Not
Rated” (NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5.
This classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet
provide a suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-
established players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR.
Players classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most
appropriately reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches
and establish a more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged
to consult with a local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or
knowledgeable team captain for guidance regarding appropriate division
placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.
4.5. Players with a DUPR Rating of "NR" (Not Rated): Players with a DUPR rating of NR (Not

6.2.3.6. DUPR Posting: All gender-based games will be submitted and posted to the

Teams are numbered 1–3 for Men’s Doubles, 4–6 for Women’s Doubles, and 7–12 for Mixed

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Incomplete Matches
allCandidates.content:
5.8. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.8.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.8.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.8.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.content:
6.3. PrimeTime DUPR League
The PrimeTime DUPR League is exclusively for players age 65 and older who want
competitive play against others in the same age group. Using DUPR's 65+ age-based rating
system, the league provides a more level playing field by matching players of similar age and
ability. Separate men's and women's divisions compete weekly with two doubles teams
representing each squad, and any tied team match is decided by the exciting Picklebreaker
format. PrimeTime emphasizes spirited competition, sportsmanship, and the opportunity
for experienced players to continue enjoying high-quality league play in a community-
focused environment.
Player Age Eligibility: A player’s age for league eligibility shall be determined by the age
they will attain as of December 31 of the current calendar year. A player is considered
age-eligible for the entire season even if they have not yet reached the required age by the
season’s start date.

5.15.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).
5.15.2. PlayoƯs feature the top 4 teams per Division based on the LMS points; ties are
settled by Line/Game Win %, then point diƯerential, and finally a coin flip. For
divisions with 2 pools, the top 2 teams from each pool advance to playoƯs.
5.15.3. PlayoƯs will take place the week following the last regular season games, with all
games played at one location.

regular season.
5.15.6. A round-robin format will be implemented instead of traditional matchups: players
in Line 1 will compete against all other players in Line 1, and similarly, players in
additional lines will compete against all other players in their respective lines.
5.15.7. Every win earns one point, and overall points determine Gold, Silver, and Bronze
team winners. Ties are broken by regular season standings; the higher seed
wins.
5.15.8. All Championship Day games will be posted to DUPR but not recorded in the LMS.
5.15.9. Gold / 1st place division teams are named the Season’s Division Champions based
on Championship Day results, not regular-season standings alone.

allCandidates.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
allCandidates.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.

separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
allCandidates.content:
ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
o The home team captain must enter all scores into the LMS within 24 hours of completing the
games. If both captains agree beforehand, the visiting team captain may enter the scores
instead.
 Entering Match Scores: To enter scores, click the Enter Match Scores button in the
match. This option becomes available only on or after the scheduled match date and
will be red.
 Forfeits and Weather Delays: If an entire match date is forfeited or canceled due to
weather, notify League Management. They will log the information for that match and
update the standings.
 Score Entry Process: When entering scores, use the dropdown menus to select the
players for each game (built from your Match Setup), then enter the scores in each
game block. Click Submit when finished; the system will check for errors before saving.
 Score Verification: Once scores are submitted, the opposing captain will receive an
email request to verify them, and a red notification count will appear in their Pending
Match Verifications block. The opposing captain must open the match, review the
scores, and click the verification button (or dispute button if they don’t accept the
scores as written). Both captains will then be notified, and the standings will update
automatically.
o The visiting team captain must verify match scores promptly. This ensures there is enough time
to review the results and enter them into DUPR before the end of the weekend.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: VIEW SCHEDULE/GAME INFORMATION
allCandidates.content:
VIEW SCHEDULE/GAME INFORMATION
o On the Captain Dashboard, the selected team’s “next match” will be displayed along with
options for that match.
o Match Setup & Lineups: Captains must enter their lineups before match day to verify player
and team ratings. For complete details, see the Team/Game Rules in the DUPR League Rules.
o Completed Matches: Scroll down to the Recent results section to review score details for
past matches. Click on a match to see all detailed results including players and individual game
scores.
o Court Reservations & Match Details: The home team captain must reserve the required
number of courts for warm-ups and match play. You should confirm the start time and share all
location details with the visiting captain beforehand by clicking the Email Opposing Captains
button.
o Finding Captain Contact Info: Click the Division Captains button in the Captain Tools block
to view or print contact details for all captains and co-captains in your division.

Quick Start Guide
As a player, you can use the League Management System to view your team schedules,
standings, match details, and club DUPR information.
If you belong to multiple teams, use the My Teams option in the sidebar to select which
team's dashboard and information you want to view.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.
Understanding DUPR Ratings

finalTop.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
finalTop.content:
6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date

Rated” (NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5.
This classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet
provide a suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-
established players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR.
Players classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most
appropriately reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches
and establish a more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged
to consult with a local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or
knowledgeable team captain for guidance regarding appropriate division
placement.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.content:
6.3. PrimeTime DUPR League
The PrimeTime DUPR League is exclusively for players age 65 and older who want
competitive play against others in the same age group. Using DUPR's 65+ age-based rating
system, the league provides a more level playing field by matching players of similar age and
ability. Separate men's and women's divisions compete weekly with two doubles teams
representing each squad, and any tied team match is decided by the exciting Picklebreaker
format. PrimeTime emphasizes spirited competition, sportsmanship, and the opportunity
for experienced players to continue enjoying high-quality league play in a community-
focused environment.
Player Age Eligibility: A player’s age for league eligibility shall be determined by the age
they will attain as of December 31 of the current calendar year. A player is considered
age-eligible for the entire season even if they have not yet reached the required age by the
season’s start date.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: LEAGUES
allCandidates.content:
6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

regular season.
6.3.14. A round-robin format will be implemented instead of traditional matchups: players
in Line 1 will compete against all other players in Line 1, and similarly, players in
additional lines will compete against all other players in their respective lines.

Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
The schedule uses two courts for men’s teams and two courts for women’s teams. After the first four
gender-doubles rounds, Men’s Team 3 and Women’s Team 6 play while Mixed Teams 7 and 8 begin.
Round 6 includes the remaining mixed teams. If the match is tied 12-12 after all gender and mixed
doubles, the Picklebreaker is played on two courts using the same mixed teams in the captains’
designated order.

Quick Start Guide
As a player, you can use the League Management System to view your team schedules,
standings, match details, and club DUPR information.
If you belong to multiple teams, use the My Teams option in the sidebar to select which
team's dashboard and information you want to view.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.
Understanding DUPR Ratings
Season DUPR ratings are displayed throughout the system. To learn how DUPR ratings are
calculated, visit this website: https://www.dupr.com/how-it-works. For questions about
how the Club uses DUPR ratings, which rating is used, or other DUPR-related topics, contact
[official contact omitted].

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Incomplete Matches
allCandidates.content:
5.8. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.8.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.8.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.8.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.content:
6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Forfeits
allCandidates.content:
6.3.7. Forfeits: In the event of a forfeit (unable to reschedule and not weather related),
the match score is officially recorded as 3-0 in favor of the non-forfeiting team.
6.3.8. Weather Issues: If games are aƯected by weather-related issues and both teams
are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe, the
matches will officially be scored as a “weather related” resulting in a 2-2 tie.
DUPR League Summary

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
allCandidates.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: SCORING & RECORDING
allCandidates.content:
2. SCORING & RECORDING
2.1. Picklebreaker games are not posted to DUPR because of their format; bonus points are
automatically added to the winning team’s total. When entering game results, simply enter
the ending scores. This will not aƯect any individual players’ win/loss records.

allCandidates.heading: PrimeTime DUPR League Key Dates
allCandidates.content:
PrimeTime DUPR League Key Dates
• Sept. 7, Monday – Open Registration
• Sept. 27, Sunday – Season DUPR ratings recorded
• Sept. 28, Monday - Can start updating rosters
• Oct. 4, Sunday – Last day to register (4 weeks)
• Oct. 7, Wednesday – Schedules completed and sent
• Oct. 16 - PrimeTime League Starts
• Nov. 25/26 Break Week
• Dec. 4 - PrimeTime League Regular Season Ends
• Dec. 11 - PrimeTime League Championship Day
Note: No games the week of Nov. 22 (Thanksgiving Break)

Player Eligibility & DUPR Ratings
Click the Add Player button to add a player to your roster.
• Selection: A pop-up window will appear with your home community preselected.
Use the drop-down menu to view available players, along with their eligibility status
and DUPR ratings.
• Missing DUPR Info: If a player is missing a DUPR ID or Season Rating, select the
player and click Add Player to Team. League Management will automatically be
notified to review the issue and update you on their status.
• Ineligible Players: If a player is marked "Not Eligible," attempting to add them will
display an on-screen message explaining the specific reason why.
Add Player Pop-up Window

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: DUPR LEAGUE MANAGERS
allCandidates.content:
DUPR LEAGUE MANAGERS
Team captains should first attempt to resolve disputes directly, relying on common sense and
fair play. If they cannot reach an agreement, or if further issues arise during the season, DUPR
League Managers will review the matter. All decisions by DUPR League Managers are final and
cannot be appealed.
For questions or concerns, please reach out to one of the following DUPR League Managers:
• [official contact omitted] – DUPR League Co-Chair > [official contact omitted]
• Bill Weihs – DUPR League Co-Chair > [official contact omitted]

team winners. Ties are broken by regular season standings; the higher seed wins,
then by point diƯerential between the tied teams, and finally a coin flip.
6.3.16. All Championship Day games will be posted to DUPR but not recorded in the LMS.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Scheduling
allCandidates.content:
6.3.1. Scheduling: Women’s and men’s games are typically scheduled for Fridays at
noon.
6.3.2. Roster & Courts: 4 players / 2 lines. Requires 2 courts. Player age is determined as
of 12/31 of the season’s starting year. Players must be 65 or older and will use the
DUPR Age-Based Rating. Players who are under age 65 at the start of the season
but will turn 65 by December 31 of the current calendar year shall be considered
Not Rated (NR) for purposes of their Season DUPR Rating, as they will not yet have
an official 65+ age-based DUPR rating at the start of the season.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.content:
5.15. End of Season PlayoƯs/Championship Day (All Leagues)
5.15.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).
5.15.2. PlayoƯs feature the top 4 teams per Division based on the LMS points; ties are
settled by Line/Game Win %, then point diƯerential, and finally a coin flip. For
divisions with 2 pools, the top 2 teams from each pool advance to playoƯs.
5.15.3. PlayoƯs will take place the week following the last regular season games, with all
games played at one location.
5.15.4. Captains will form teams following regular season rules and Season DUPR ratings.
5.15.5. Players may participate in a Division end-of-season/Championship game only if
they have competed in at least one game within that Division during the current
regular season.
5.15.6. A round-robin format will be implemented instead of traditional matchups: players
in Line 1 will compete against all other players in Line 1, and similarly, players in
additional lines will compete against all other players in their respective lines.
5.15.7. Every win earns one point, and overall points determine Gold, Silver, and Bronze
team winners. Ties are broken by regular season standings; the higher seed
wins.
5.15.8. All Championship Day games will be posted to DUPR but not recorded in the LMS.
5.15.9. Gold / 1st place division teams are named the Season’s Division Champions based
on Championship Day results, not regular-season standings alone.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: TEAM ORDER & ROTATION
allCandidates.content:
1. TEAM ORDER & ROTATION
1.1. Captains will create doubles teams from the current players and designate play order
including abiding by all DUPR team rating/division rules.

Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
[official contact omitted].
Match Setup Window

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: PLAYER REQUIREMENTS
allCandidates.content:
3. PLAYER REQUIREMENTS
3.1. All League players must have a signed/accepted waiver with LWR PC and have a valid
LWR PC membership. To sign up, go to https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup/.
3.2. All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be found at:
https://www.dupr.com/.
3.3. All DUPR League players must join our free DUPR club, which is diƯerent/separate from
the LWR PC membership: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB
3.4. Players are assigned to a community based on their primary address at the start of the
season.
3.5. Players may join teams from other communities; however, they are strongly encouraged
to play for their local community’s team when their community has a team participating in
the same league and division with available roster space.

finalTop.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
finalTop.heading: DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
finalTop.content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor of 29 or below will be classified as “Not
Rated” (NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5.
This classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet
provide a suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-
established players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR.
Players classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most
appropriately reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches
and establish a more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged
to consult with a local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or
knowledgeable team captain for guidance regarding appropriate division
placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.

selected.heading: DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
selected.content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor of 29 or below will be classified as “Not
Rated” (NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5.
This classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet
provide a suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-
established players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR.
Players classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most
appropriately reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches
and establish a more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged
to consult with a local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or
knowledgeable team captain for guidance regarding appropriate division
placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: CAPTAINS NORMAL WEEKLY PROCESS
allCandidates.content:
CAPTAINS NORMAL WEEKLY PROCESS
o Captain Match Duties: For every match, captains or co-captains must set their lineup (Match
Setup), print the score sheet, and enter or validate final scores.
o Lineup Submission: Both captains must enter starting lineups in Match Setup at least 3 days
before match day. It is recommended that the Home Team enter their lineups first.
 Updates: You can modify your lineup until match day. The system automatically emails
changes to the opposing captain.
 Penalties: Repeated incomplete or late lineup submissions may result in match
forfeiture, subject to League Management discretion.
o Match Score Sheet: Once both teams have entered their lineups in the League Management
System (LMS), the official Match Score Sheet may be printed. Captains can access the Match
Score Sheet button from the “Next Match” section of their Captain Dashboard.
 The completed Match Score Sheet will include all available match information,
including player names, team information, and game formats. If either team has not
entered its lineup, that team’s lineup information will appear blank on the score
sheet.
 The LMS-generated Match Score Sheet is the official score sheet and must be used
for each scheduled match. Captains should retain all completed Match Score
Sheets for the duration of the season as a backup record of match results.

Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
[official contact omitted].
Match Setup Window

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
allCandidates.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
allCandidates.content:
ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
o The home team captain must enter all scores into the LMS within 24 hours of completing the
games. If both captains agree beforehand, the visiting team captain may enter the scores
instead.
 Entering Match Scores: To enter scores, click the Enter Match Scores button in the
match. This option becomes available only on or after the scheduled match date and
will be red.
 Forfeits and Weather Delays: If an entire match date is forfeited or canceled due to
weather, notify League Management. They will log the information for that match and
update the standings.
 Score Entry Process: When entering scores, use the dropdown menus to select the
players for each game (built from your Match Setup), then enter the scores in each
game block. Click Submit when finished; the system will check for errors before saving.
 Score Verification: Once scores are submitted, the opposing captain will receive an
email request to verify them, and a red notification count will appear in their Pending
Match Verifications block. The opposing captain must open the match, review the
scores, and click the verification button (or dispute button if they don’t accept the
scores as written). Both captains will then be notified, and the standings will update
automatically.
o The visiting team captain must verify match scores promptly. This ensures there is enough time
to review the results and enter them into DUPR before the end of the weekend.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
allCandidates.heading: CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
allCandidates.content:
CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
Each League team must have a designated Captain. A Captain may also serve as Co-Captain on
another team and may captain a team in the opposite gender category. However, a person may not
captain more than one team within the same gender category. There can be up to two Co-Captains.
Community Team Captains and Co-Captains have “Captain” access to the League Management
System (LMS) at league.lwrpickleballclub.com to manage teams, rosters, schedules, scores, and
overall league information. (For general club details, visit the main website at lwrpickleballclub.com).
Captains are responsible for their team roster, each match date setup including reserving all home
courts, recording/validating scores and general team management. Club League Management is
available at any time for help with any questions or concerns. See last page for contact information.
Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to host their share
of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability, resulting in a balanced home-
and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot reserve enough courts for all its assigned
home match dates, additional matches may be scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to
provide any courts due to limitations within their community or facility will play all their scheduled
matches as away games.
All league players also have access to the LMS through their personal Player Dashboard, where they
can view their assigned teams, upcoming and completed matches, team rosters, and standings. It also
features a full personal play history and quick-click shortcuts to email team captains. Captains can
also switch to the Player Dashboard to see their personal league information.

allCandidates.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Scoresheet Annotations
allCandidates.content:
17.D.6 Scoresheet Annotations. Appropriately annotate the scoresheet
after a rally is completed or a time-out is called.

Captain Dashboard Overview
Use the dashboard to overall manage your team(s), keep on top of all upcoming and prior
matches, manage rosters, view standings, and handle score tasks. If you captain multiple
teams, select the correct team under My Team in the sidebar to update the view.
Dashboard Highlights:
• Top Navigation: At the very top right of the Captain Dashboard, you can access the
Captain User Guide, email the league, or click the button next to your name to
update your profile, change your password, adjust appearance settings, or view your
club membership.
• Sidebar Options: Click League Documents to view all available files for your
league.
• Quick Links/Captain Toolbar: Access your team list, manage your team and see
your division schedules and division captain contacts.
• Team Information: Your main dashboard gives you quick access to your next
match—complete with quick-action buttons for match setup. You can also monitor
your team's current rank, record, and any pending score entry or validations,
alongside quick-view sections for division standings, upcoming schedules, and
recent match results.
Main Captain Dashboard Screen (Desktop View)

Entering Match Scores
Captains enter scores, record forfeits, and confirm official match results. When entering
scores, normally select the “Use this saved team” pulldown to display the previously
entered Match Setup team. If there were changes to that, simply select the correct player in
the individual player pulldown option.
• Game Forfeits & Retirements: Refer to the official League Rules when entering
results for individual games impacted by player or play-related issues.
• Full Match Cancellations: If an entire match date is forfeited or cannot be played
due to weather or scheduling conflicts, do not enter it into the system. Instead,
contact League Management at [official contact omitted].
• Eligible/Ineligible Player: In actual score entry, the same eligibility rules apply to
the players entered for each game line. An ineligible player cannot be selected, and
score fields are blocked if that line has an eligibility issue.
Enter Match Scores Screen

allCandidates.heading: VIEW SCHEDULE/GAME INFORMATION
allCandidates.content:
VIEW SCHEDULE/GAME INFORMATION
o On the Captain Dashboard, the selected team’s “next match” will be displayed along with
options for that match.
o Match Setup & Lineups: Captains must enter their lineups before match day to verify player
and team ratings. For complete details, see the Team/Game Rules in the DUPR League Rules.
o Completed Matches: Scroll down to the Recent results section to review score details for
past matches. Click on a match to see all detailed results including players and individual game
scores.
o Court Reservations & Match Details: The home team captain must reserve the required
number of courts for warm-ups and match play. You should confirm the start time and share all
location details with the visiting captain beforehand by clicking the Email Opposing Captains
button.
o Finding Captain Contact Info: Click the Division Captains button in the Captain Tools block
to view or print contact details for all captains and co-captains in your division.

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: Match Setup and Roster Exchange
allCandidates.content:
5.5. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within
the required timeframe may result in forfeiture of the current or future matches, at the
discretion of League Management.

Upcoming Matches
Your Next Match appears at the top of the Captain Dashboard. From this section, captains
can view match details, email the opposing captains, print Match Score Sheet and enter final
scores. If this is a “flex league” you are also able to modify the match date/time and notify
opposing captains.
You can also manage your match lineup and score sheets here:
• Match Setup block: The Match Setup button turns red if your team hasn't entered
its lineup yet, and blue once you have. The system will email you a reminder to
complete this a few days before the actual match.
• Print Match Score Sheet button: Stays red until both teams complete their Match
Setup, turning green and ready to print once both lineups are in.
The Upcoming matches & byes section shows all upcoming match details, scheduling
information, and setup status. You can also click on a match for all available tools/options
for that match.
Upcoming / Unverified Matches Screen

allCandidates.heading: Point Scoring
allCandidates.content: Section 4 Point Scoring

Submitting Scores
Clicking Submit Scores saves the match results only when all player, team, and score
information is valid according to division rules. You cannot save any of the results (partial
save) if any information is invalid.
Once submitted:
• Notifications: The system automatically emails the opposing captains to notify
them that the scores have been entered.
• Verification: If your team is the first to enter the results, a captain of the opposing
team must log in to verify or dispute the scores to finalize the match and update the
league/division standings.
Score Verification Process
Use Pending Verification to review entered scores or raise disputes.
Selecting the appropriate button will:
• Finalize Results: Complete the scoring process for the match.
• Notify Captains: Automatically email all captains to confirm the match date and
scores are officially entered and locked.
• Update Standings: Instantly refresh the league/division standings.
Captain Dashboard / Pending Score Verification (red)

2.1. Picklebreaker games are not posted to DUPR because of their format; bonus points are

Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
DUPR League Captains Guide
Welcome to the Captain & Co-Captain Guide! Think of this as your go-to manual for standard team
management and captain duties.
As a Captain or Co-Captain, we appreciate your commitment to both your community and your team
members. Your position is vital to the success of our League as well as to those you lead. We are here to
support you in fulfilling these responsibilities, and this guide has been prepared to oƯer comprehensive
answers and guidance to help facilitate your role as Captain/Co-Captain.
A reminder about two additional key documents that all Captains should review and be familiar with:

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.content:
5.15. End of Season PlayoƯs/Championship Day (All Leagues)
5.15.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).
5.15.2. PlayoƯs feature the top 4 teams per Division based on the LMS points; ties are
settled by Line/Game Win %, then point diƯerential, and finally a coin flip. For
divisions with 2 pools, the top 2 teams from each pool advance to playoƯs.
5.15.3. PlayoƯs will take place the week following the last regular season games, with all
games played at one location.
5.15.4. Captains will form teams following regular season rules and Season DUPR ratings.
5.15.5. Players may participate in a Division end-of-season/Championship game only if
they have competed in at least one game within that Division during the current
regular season.
5.15.6. A round-robin format will be implemented instead of traditional matchups: players
in Line 1 will compete against all other players in Line 1, and similarly, players in
additional lines will compete against all other players in their respective lines.
5.15.7. Every win earns one point, and overall points determine Gold, Silver, and Bronze
team winners. Ties are broken by regular season standings; the higher seed
wins.
5.15.8. All Championship Day games will be posted to DUPR but not recorded in the LMS.
5.15.9. Gold / 1st place division teams are named the Season’s Division Champions based
on Championship Day results, not regular-season standings alone.

DUPR LEAGUE RULES
• The DUPR League Mission and League Rules contain the official policies and requirements for
team creation, player eligibility, roster requirements, and specific rules for each of our leagues.
You can access the most current version of this document at any time by logging into the LMS and

allCandidates.heading: Tournament Event and Scoring
allCandidates.content:
Section 15 Tournament Event and Scoring
Options

allCandidates.heading: Scoring for Game Forfeit
allCandidates.content:
22.H Scoring for Game Forfeit. When a game forfeit is imposed on a singles
player or doubles team, their score for the forfeited game must be
reported as zero (e.g., 11-0 for a game to 11 points, 15-0 for a game to 15
points, or 21-0 for a game to 21 points). Scores for games completed
before the forfeited game are retained. (See Rule 15.B.4.a for a round
robin.)

allCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
allCandidates.heading: CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
allCandidates.content:
1. CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
1.1. Club main website: https://lwrpickleballclub.com
1.2. League Management System (LMS) website: https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com
1.3. There are three seasons: Fall, Winter, and Spring.

finalTop.documentTitle: LWRPC-Captains Guide to the LMS
finalTop.content:

Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.

type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.

repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.

DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.

completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.

captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.

LEAGUE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (LMS) – Login Instructions
The League Management System is located at https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com. Enter your
email address and password to sign in. We recommend bookmarking this page, as it will serve
as your main go-to page for all League information and activities throughout the season.
 First-Time Users: Enter the email address associated with your Club Membership and
click Forgot Password. A setup or a password reset email will be sent from no-
[official contact omitted] to create your password. If you aren't sure which

Match Score Sheet

player names, and the format of play. You are able to print this if both teams have not
completed their Match Setup but those teams not completed will be blank.
• Button Color: Stays red until both teams enter their lineups, turning green once
both setups are complete.
• Printing: Print the sheet only after the button turns green. Printing early will leave
missing lineups blank.
• Scoring: Use the printed sheet to record scores during the match, then enter the
final results into the system after all games are complete.
• Retention: Keep all completed physical sheets for the entire season in case the
league needs them for reference.
Email Opposing Captains
Click Email Opposing Captains to quickly message all captains on the opposing team.
Selecting this button opens your default email program and automatically populates the
match details, allowing you to type your message and send it directly.

allCandidates.heading: Damaged Ball

ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines

allCandidates.heading: Ball Selection
allCandidates.content:
16.G Ball Selection. The Tournament Director will choose the tournament ball
from the official list of approved balls posted on the USA Pickleball website.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Specifications
allCandidates.content:
3.C Ball Specifications. The requirements for the ball are set forth in Rules 3.C.1
through 3.C.5. The complete list of approved balls is posted on the USA
Pickleball website.

allCandidates.heading: 24.B Extra Ball — Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls
allCandidates.content:
24.B.1 Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls. When an extra ball
carried by a player is visible to an opponent or falls to the
playing surface while the ball is live, it is a fault against the
player.

allCandidates.heading: Returned Ball Placement
allCandidates.content:
10.C Returned Ball Placement. A player must return the ball so that the ball
lands on the opponent’s end of the court or contacts the opponent or
anything that is worn or carried by the opponent before the ball lands.

allCandidates.heading: 13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net — Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side
allCandidates.content:
13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side. When a ball bounces in the
court on the receiving player’s end of the net and then returns to
the opponent’s side of the net without being hit, the receiving
player may cross over, under, or around the net to hit the ball, but
only after the ball has first crossed back to the opponent’s end of
the net.

allCandidates.heading: 7.B Ball Release — No Manipulation or Spin Upon Release
allCandidates.content:
7.B.2 No Manipulation or Spin Upon Release. Some natural rotation of
the ball is expected during any release of the ball. The server must
not manipulate the ball to add spin with any part of the server's
body or the paddle prior to hitting the ball to make the serve,
except that the server may allow the ball to roll off the face of the
paddle by gravity. Spin may be applied to the ball upon contact by
the paddle.

allCandidates.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
allCandidates.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

allCandidates.heading: 13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net — After Hitting the Ball
allCandidates.content:
13.I.1 After Hitting the Ball. A player may cross the plane of the net
immediately after hitting the ball. The allowance to cross the plane
of the net only applies while executing the current strike of the ball
and for continuation associated with the current strike of the ball.

allCandidates.heading: Damaged Ball
allCandidates.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net
allCandidates.content:
13.A Ball Contacting Net. When the ball contacts the net, or the rope or cable at
the top of the net between the net posts, the ball remains in play.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net Support System
allCandidates.content:
13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System. A served ball must not contact any
part of the net support system. A returned ball must not contact any part of
the net support system on the hitting player’s end of the net.

allCandidates.heading: 22.D Technical Fouls — Ball Abuse
allCandidates.content:
22.D.2 Ball Abuse. Aggressively or recklessly throwing or hitting a dead
ball in frustration or anger with negligent disregard for the
consequences as long as the ball does not strike a person but
puts a person at risk or in danger.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Crossing Plane of Net
allCandidates.content:
13.F Ball Crossing Plane of Net. A ball must entirely cross to a player’s end of
the net before the player hits the ball.

allCandidates.heading: “In” Ball
allCandidates.content:
8.B “In” Ball. A served ball that clears the opponent’s non-volley zone line and
lands in the correct service court is “in.” A ball returned by a player that
lands on the opponent’s end of the court is “in.”

allCandidates.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Ball Height
allCandidates.content:
7.C.3 Ball Height. The ball must clearly be no higher than the server’s
waist when the paddle contacts the ball.

allCandidates.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
allCandidates.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

allCandidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Dead Ball
allCandidates.content:
25.B.3.d Dead Ball. When the ball strikes a permanent object
(e.g., fence, wall) before the second bounce, it is a
dead ball and the rally ends.

allCandidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
allCandidates.content:
10.G.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When all players agree that a
broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the rally
must be replayed. If all players do not agree that a broken or
cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the result of the rally
stands.

allCandidates.heading: “Out” Ball
allCandidates.content:
8.C “Out” Ball. A served ball that does not land in the correct service court on
the opponent’s end of the court, including one that lands on the non-volley
zone line, is “out.” Any other ball that lands outside the court is “out.”

allCandidates.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System
allCandidates.content:
13.B.2 Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System. When a returned
ball crosses the net and contacts any part of a crossbar, or any
other part of the net support system within the court boundaries,
before or after the ball bounces, the rally must be replayed.

allCandidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing
allCandidates.content:
10.C.5 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing. When a player
fails to return a ball that has bounced in the player’s court before
the ball contacts a permanent object, it is a fault against that
player.

allCandidates.heading: 13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side — Fault – Ball Not Contacted
allCandidates.content:
13.I.2.b Fault – Ball Not Contacted. When a ball bounces in
the court on the receiving player’s end of the net and
then returns to the opponent’s end of the net without
being hit, it is a fault against a player who fails to hit
the ball before it bounces once on the opponent’s end
of the net.

allCandidates.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Fault – Ball Contacts Net Support System
allCandidates.content:
13.B.1 Fault – Ball Contacts Net Support System. When a player serves a
ball that contacts the net support system on either end of the net
or returns a ball that contacts the net support system before going
over the net, it is a fault against the player.

allCandidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Ball Release Not Visible
allCandidates.content:
20.E.2.a Replay – Ball Release Not Visible. When it is
questionable whether the release of the ball was not
visible to the referee and receiver, the referee may
call for a replay. When the referee is certain that the
release of the ball was not visible, the referee must
call for a replay.

allCandidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Usage
allCandidates.content:
3.C.1 Usage. All approved balls are acceptable for indoor or outdoor
play. (See Figure 3-2.)

allCandidates.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Ball Abuse
allCandidates.content:
22.B.4 Ball Abuse. Intentionally damaging or aggressively hitting a
dead ball without endangering people.

allCandidates.heading: 13.F Ball Crossing Plane of Net — Fault – Ball Hit Before Crossing Plane of Net
allCandidates.content:
13.F.1 Fault – Ball Hit Before Crossing Plane of Net. When a player hits
the ball before the ball entirely crosses the plane of the net to the
player’s end, it is a fault against the player.

allCandidates.heading: Extra Ball
allCandidates.content:
24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

allCandidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
allCandidates.content:
20.E.2.i Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
When it is questionable whether the ball was
propelled when the server released the ball to make
a drop serve, the referee must call for a replay.

allCandidates.heading: Ball Release
allCandidates.content:
7.B Ball Release. The server must comply with Rules 7.B.1 through 7.B.3 when
releasing the ball to make the serve.

finalTop.documentTitle: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
finalTop.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Construction
finalTop.content:
3.C.5 Construction. The ball must be made of durable material molded
with a smooth surface and free of texturing. The ball may have a
slight ridge at the seam, as long as it does not significantly impact
the ball’s flight characteristics. (See Figure 3-2.)
The ball with larger holes is customarily used
for indoor play (pictured on the left). The ball
with smaller holes is customarily used for
outdoor play (pictured on the right).
Figure 3-2: Approved Balls – Examples

finalTop.documentTitle: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
finalTop.heading: Damaged Ball
finalTop.content:
20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a
ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

finalTop.documentTitle: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
finalTop.heading: Ball Selection
finalTop.content:
16.G Ball Selection. The Tournament Director will choose the tournament ball
from the official list of approved balls posted on the USA Pickleball website.

originalTop.heading: LEAGUE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (LMS) - (CAPTAINS USER GUIDE)
originalTop.content:

• Captains User Guide: Everything you need to run your team in the LMS—from roster management
and match setup to score entry and standings tracking. For step-by-step technical instructions on
using the LMS, log in and click the Captains User Guide (question mark icon) in the top header.
• Getting Started: “League Management System (LMS) – Login Instructions” (Page 6) – Provides
step-by-step instructions specifically for logging into the League Management System for the first
time.

originalTop.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
originalTop.heading: Match Setup and Roster Exchange
originalTop.content:
5.5. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within
the required timeframe may result in forfeiture of the current or future matches, at the
discretion of League Management.

originalTop.documentTitle: LWRPC-Captains Guide to the LMS
originalTop.content:
Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
[official contact omitted].
Match Setup Window
